question.problem: Use Green's theorem to evaluate ${∮}_{C}(2xy-{y}^{2})\,dx+({x}^{2}+2x)\,dy,$ where $C$ is the boundary of the triangle with vertices at $(-1,0),$ $(1,0)$ and $(-1,2).$
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14223852/assets/cb85e51584f0c41fc19210a5ce56289baa652aff3046d5d88c034d187b7e45dd.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=2xy-{y}^{2}$ and $Q(x,y)={x}^{2}+2x.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=2x-2y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x} & =2x+2.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1-x\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}(2xy-{y}^{2})\,dx+({x}^{2}+2x)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2x+2-2x+2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2+2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}(2+2y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{[2y+{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{1-x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(2(1-x)+(1-x)^{2})dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}({x}^{2}-4x+3)\,dx \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-2{x}^{2}+3x]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =[\frac{1}{3}-2+3]-[-\frac{1}{3}-2-3] \\  & =\frac{2}{3}+6 \\  & =\frac{20}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
